data.gender_notes: Parash is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘पराश्पति’ (Parashpati), meaning 'Lord of the Gods'. In Hindu mythology, Parashpati is a god of wealth and knowledge, and is also known as the god of healing. The name Parash carries the meaning “Lord” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Parash usually hope their child will grow to embody lord and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of divine wisdom and prosperity.
data.etymology: Parash belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Parash total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: Parashpati, as a name, holds deep cultural significance in the Hindu tradition. It represents the divine grace and protection of the gods. It is believed that invoking this name brings good luck, prosperity, and knowledge. In various Hindu rituals and ceremonies, the name Parashpati is chanted to invoke the blessings of the gods, specifically for success and good fortune.
data.spiritual_significance: Parashpati is also seen as a symbol of spiritual enlightenment and wisdom. In Hindu spirituality, it is believed that through the grace of Parashpati, an individual can gain immense knowledge and understanding of the universe and attain liberation from the cycle of birth and death. Parashpati is revered as a teacher and healer, remedying not only physical ailments but also the emotional and spiritual wounds of an individual. This name therefore holds deep spiritual significance, representing the divine guidance and protection of the gods on the journey towards self-realization and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Parash, meaning 'destroyer of obstacles', represents the divine power that removes all barriers and challenges in the path of spiritual growth and self-realization. It symbolizes the inner strength and determination to overcome life's hurdles and emerge victorious.

vedic_reference.note: Parash is derived from the Sanskrit word 'paras' meaning 'beyond' or 'surpassing'. It is not directly mentioned in any Vedic texts, but the concept of going beyond the limits is present in various Vedic teachings.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Parash is a name mentioned in the Mahabharata, the great Indian epic. The name Parash carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Parash is a charioteer of Arjuna, the greatest of the Pandava princes.
